signature: export function restrictedCoordinates(d: SatakeDiagram, rb: RestrictedBoard, shadow2: Vec<number>): number[]  // satake.ts, exported by name from src/index.ts, listed in PHASE_6_NAMES. Order of checks: d's shape (RangeError), shadow2's length and integer entries (RangeError), rb belongs to d (its orbits are exactly the tau-orbits of d's white positions and each simple restricted root has n integer entries; RangeError), then requireGcm and requireFinite (NeedsTwoWayRoads, NotFiniteType). Method: exact normal equations G c = S v in bigint, solved with linalg.solve over Rational, then the combination checked exactly against shadow2. RangeError 'is not a combination of the simple restricted roots', 'is not zero, but this diagram has no simple restricted root (a compact form ...)', 'is not an integer combination ...: its coordinates would be (1/2, 0)'. Admissibility is not judged again (rb only comes from restrictedBoard). Pure; no side effects at the module's top level.

handoff: For P6-A3 (T13). Import restrictedCoordinates by name from '@engine'. If you route it through engineCall, provide({ restrictedCoordinates }) as P6-size requires. Call restrictedCoordinates(d, rb, shadow2(d, root)) with rb = restrictedBoard(d) for the same diagram, positions throughout. It computes no roots and no w_X word, so it is cheap per root on the main thread. Keep rb in step with the decoration: an rb from another diagram throws RangeError. The result has one integer per orbit, in the order of rb.orbits (the same order as rb.simpleRestrictedRoots2, rb.cartan and rb.board's positions). These are the coordinates of the shadow itself in the simple restricted roots, so the double of a BC root has coordinate 2. A compact form gives []. To show a value on the drawn restricted board (boardFromName of the name after satakeRecord's C2 rename, where the node labelled j stands for record.restricted_orbits_in_bourbaki_order[j-1] in big-board labels), find k with toLabels(board, rb.orbits[k]) equal to that orbit and show coords[k]. Without the C2 rename this is the same as k = toPositions(rb.board, [j])[0], since rb.board.labels[k] === j. On su(2,2), sp(4,R), sp(2,2) and so*(8) the drawn C2 lists the two orbits reversed, so always match by orbit, never by rb.board.labels. A click on drawn node j plays rb.compositeWords[k] (the same k) on the population. The new coordinates are restrictedCoordinates(d, rb, shadow2(d, newRoot)), which equals mutate(rb.board, coords, k); this was tested on all 135 records. Worked example e6(-26): alpha_6 gives [0, 1] (orbits [[1], [6]], A2 labels [1, 2]), and node 2 makes it [0, -1]. For the coordinate text, halve nothing: the shadow is the halves vector and the coordinates are integers. A fraction can only come from a vector that is not a shadow; that throws RangeError, and the message lists the fractions.
